assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single DNA and RNA molecules as ionic-current blockades through a nanopore rests on a clean physical principle, and Oxford Nanopore devices now sequence long reads in the field. The idea moved from physical insight to a deployed analytical tool, which is the generative capability I weight most.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brandin, Branton and Deamer (1996) showed polynucleotides translocate an alpha-hemolysin pore; Deamer and Branton conceived sequencing; Bayley engineered pores and adapters; Akeson showed base discrimination and enzyme-controlled ratcheting. A three-person split of Deamer, Akeson and Bayley is defensible, but Branton and Kasianowicz have strong claims and the split is contested.
assessment.maturity: Commercial sequencing is more than a decade old and has been reproduced by many independent groups. Accuracy and throughput keep improving, so timing is good.
uncertainties: The current eligibility of some credited individuals (living status) is not verified by me.
Branton's and Kasianowicz's claims are left out of a three-name configuration.
Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or as biophysics and technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1991 dye-sensitized nanocrystalline cell separated light absorption from charge transport using a mesoporous TiO2 film with a molecular sensitizer. It is a clear physical-chemical design principle, and it opened mesoscopic photovoltaics and the later perovskite cells.
assessment.attribution: O'Regan and Grätzel's 1991 Nature paper is the decisive contribution, and Grätzel led the sustained development of dyes and cells. Hagfeldt is a strong contributor to mechanism and later optimization but not a founding name. Two laureates give a clean citation.
assessment.maturity: Thirty-plus years of independent confirmation. Efficiencies have plateaued and commercial uptake has been modest, but the scientific impact is established and the recognition is overdue.
uncertainties: Modest commercial impact may weigh against it.
Earlier work on dye-sensitized semiconductors, which I recall only loosely, may reduce the novelty.
Whether to include Hagfeldt.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Using a small molecule to bring a target protein to an E3 ligase for ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation is a genuinely new capability. It turns binding into elimination of the protein and makes previously undruggable targets accessible, which fits the 'previously unforeseen opportunities' criterion.
assessment.attribution: Sakamoto, Kim, Crews and Deshaies (2001) gave the PROTAC concept. Ciulli made VHL ligands and structural design principles central to the field. The molecular-glue side (Handa and Ito on thalidomide and cereblon, Gray on degrader chemistry) is a separate strand that may need its own recognition or may be left out. Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli is a plausible trio.
assessment.maturity: Clinical degraders are in late-stage trials, but I know of no approved PROTAC drug, so clinical validation is still maturing. The chemistry and mechanism are widely reproduced.
uncertainties: No clear approved drug yet, so the recognition could be premature.
Credit is split between the PROTAC and molecular-glue lineages.
Sakamoto's and Kim's early roles are excluded.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1985 unified treatment of electronic structure and ion dynamics let first-principles molecular dynamics follow bond breaking and condensed-phase chemistry without a fitted force field. It is a clear and original principle, and it underlies later computational chemistry for liquids, interfaces and reactions.
assessment.attribution: Credit is cleanly two-person, Car and Parrinello. Parrinello also appears on the metadynamics and machine-learned potential candidates, so a prize here would partly cover those strands.
assessment.maturity: Forty years of use and independent validation. Timing is mature, perhaps past due.
uncertainties: Computational methods are often judged as chemistry only through their applications.
Overlap with the Parrinello candidates; whether the committee prefers a broader computational citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase turns N2 into ammonia at ambient conditions through a unique iron-molybdenum cofactor, and it is central to biological nitrogen cycling. The structures and mechanistic work attack a first-order chemical question, and the radical-chemistry insights connect to Haber-Bosch.
assessment.attribution: Rees's crystallography and Einsle's high-resolution structures with the central carbide are the structural core. Dean and Seefeldt established genetics and kinetics, and Ribbe worked on cofactor biosynthesis. A three-name list leaves out important contributors, so allocation is not clean.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well confirmed, but the full catalytic mechanism and the substrate-binding mode remain debated.
uncertainties: The mechanism is not yet settled.
Allocation among the structural, genetic and kinetic contributors is difficult.
Cofactor biosynthesis may be a separate part of the story.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors convert one base pair to another by chemical deamination on a Cas-programmed target without double-strand breaks. It is a conceptually new chemistry-on-DNA capability that is already in clinical trials, with a clear mechanistic basis.
assessment.attribution: Liu directed the work. Komor made the cytosine base editor and Gaudelli the adenine base editor through directed evolution. Nishida and Kondo's cytidine deaminase fusion was contemporaneous and could complicate the picture. Liu with Komor and Gaudelli is the cleanest fit I can offer, but the early-career names raise credit questions.
assessment.maturity: Eight to ten years old, with fast adoption and early clinical results. The 2020 CRISPR prize makes a genome-editing follow-up a harder sell, and it may be premature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 prize.
Nishida and Kondo's priority claim.
Long-term clinical validation is pending.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites reached silicon-class efficiencies in a decade, with long carrier diffusion lengths and tunable band gaps. The scientific impact is very large, but the physics of defect tolerance is still being worked out.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cell in 2009, Park and collaborators made the solid-state cell in 2012, and Snaith's group established the meso-superstructured and planar architectures. Kanatzidis and Seok are also important, and Grätzel overlaps with B005. Credit is contested.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is well replicated, but operational stability, lead toxicity and scale-up remain unresolved, so the committee may consider recognition premature.
uncertainties: Stability is unproven at scale.
Priority disputes among several groups.
Overlap with the dye-sensitized candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Folding a long scaffold strand with staple strands into arbitrary two-dimensional shapes made molecular design of nanoscale objects routine. It builds on Seeman's structural DNA nanotechnology and is relevant to my own interest in motors and molecular machines.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund's 2006 origami paper is the key origin. Yan's work on 2D and 3D lattices and Shih's 3D origami, and Yin's and Winfree's contributions, are strong, and the deceased founder Nadrian Seeman cannot be credited. Rothemund and Yan is a defensible pair, but others have good claims.
assessment.maturity: Broadly reproduced for twenty years. Applications in biosensing, lithography and computing are still emerging, so impact is more promising than proven.
uncertainties: Applications are not yet transformative.
Allocation among Rothemund, Yan, Shih, Yin and Winfree is contested.
The role of the deceased founder Seeman.
